text:
The highlight came first: a between-the-legs, top-shelf goal against Anaheim that NHL.com pitched as a goal of the season candidate. Nils Hoglander has found a fresh start in Nashville after a lost final year in Vancouver, where he managed 5 points in 38 games.

With the Predators he has 10 points (5 goals) in 22 games in a depth role, about 11.5 minutes a night, with his ice time up to 12.5 over his last ten. His own finishing is honest: five goals on 4.74 expected goals (the quality of his chances).

The on-ice results are where we'd be careful. Nashville has scored 7.32 more goals than its chances deserve with him on, and his scoring rate of 2.38 points per 60 sits above the top of our talent range for him. The good news is that the chances are real too: the Predators take 55% of the five-on-five expected goals with Hoglander out there, well above their rate without him. Evolving-Hockey's read on last season comes from a small sample (438 minutes), so this is mostly a fresh look. Watch whether the minutes keep climbing if the bounces cool.
